item.title: GT on the spot: From AI remixes to tea livestreams, young people bring fresh energy to ethnic unity in Yunnan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 21:04:00
Visitors experience the relaxed pace of life in Nuogan village on Jingmai Mountain in Pu'er, Southwest China's Yunnan Province. Photo: Li Hao/Global Times A Jingpo melody from Southwest China's Yunnan Province has found a new life on phone screens. Reworked with artificial intelligence and paired with striking dance videos, it has encouraged people far beyond its birthplace to follow the rhythm and discover the culture behind it. On Jingmai Mountain in Pu'er, another screen connects viewers with a different tradition. Xianjin, an ethnic Dai woman born in the 2000s, uses livestreams to talk about her hometown's tea, ancient forests and village life. During a recent reporting tour in Yunnan, Global Times reporter explored how younger generations are creating opportunities for exchange among ethnic groups, bringing fresh energy to efforts to forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. Lyrics of the soil At Longchuan's Munao Zongge square in Dehong Dai and Jingpo Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan, local dancers in ethnic dress and visitors form long lines, moving to the same beat. The procession brings people together in an activity they can join without being professional performers or belonging to a particular ethnic group. The viral music has deep roots, but its present form is a recent creation. Jingpo artist Shi Legan composed the "Munao Zongge March" in 1991. Earlier this year, Beijing musician Zhen Zhen adapted that melody with new lyrics and AI-assisted arrangements and vocals. Without A-list celebrities or professional promotional campaigns, the song "Munao Zongge" has garnered nearly 3 billion views on China's major short-video platform Douyin. Munao Zongge, a major Jingpo celebration featuring collective dancing, was included in China's national intangible cultural heritage list in 2006. Its winding dance formations carry memories of the Jingpo people's migration, giving today's online enthusiasm a connection to a much longer history. The name carries the idea of gathering to sing and dance. During major celebrations, participants from neighboring ethnic groups also share a meal served on banana leaves, extending the gathering from the dance ground to the dining table. For Zhen, a video of mass dancing prompted an interest that became three weeks of work. Research changed his understanding of the music: early attempts to treat it as a love song gave way to lyrics informed by Jingpo history. AI helped him arrange the music and produce virtual voices, but its research results sometimes conflicted. He went back to books and papers to check the information himself. "Lyrics have to grow out of the soil," Zhen said. In Longchuan, community dance leader Song Haihe introduced that participants include locals from different ethnic groups alongside visitors from across the country. The cultural interest also brings visitors to local businesses. Longchuan received 42,000 domestic tourist visits during this year's National Day holiday, while overnight stays in commercial accommodation rose 11.07 percent year-on-year, according to the county's culture and tourism authorities. For someone first drawn to the music through a short video, these regular gatherings provide a place to learn its steps alongside local people. The encounter can continue after the video ends. Xianjin welcomes visitors to her family's tea shop in Nuogan village. Photo: Li Hao/Global Times Connections over tea On Jingmai Mountain, Xianjin faces a related task: giving people who discover her hometown online a reason to understand it more closely. An encounter at a tea exhibition in 2020 exposed a problem she would have to overcome. When she introduced tea from her hometown, a trader asked: "Where is Jingmai Mountain?" Having a distinctive product did not guarantee that buyers knew its origins. After returning home, she began livestreaming to introduce the tea and its place of origin. Her days combine brewing tea, making tea-flavored ice cream and filming village life. She opened a tea house after seeing more visitors arrive following the mountain's World Heritage inscription in 2023. Early in her business, she realized that selling the name "Jingmai tea" was insufficient. Her videos began showing what distinguished its place of origin: clouds over the mountain, hand-processing techniques and daily life in traditional houses. The landscape behind those sales is itself a product of longstanding cooperation. UNESCO describes Jingmai Mountain's tea-growing system as having developed over more than a thousand years through the practices of the Blang and Dai peoples. Tea grows beneath a forest canopy, within a landscape of villages, groves and protective forests. Local authorities told the Global Times that the inscribed heritage area includes five old tea forests, nine traditional villages and three protective partition forests. Protecting the trees also means maintaining the communities and knowledge that have sustained them. During the reporting tour, Xianjin pointed to renovated old houses and explained that residents of different ethnic groups had worked to preserve them. The forests and village buildings were a shared inheritance. Jingmai village official Yan Sailuan described cooperation that extends from celebrations to farm work. People gather in one another's villages for festivals, contribute labor and organize long-table banquets; during tea picking and other agricultural work, neighbors help one another. Skills circulate through the same relationships. In Wengji village, tea-processing heritage practitioner Sanwen teaches learners from different villages and ethnic groups. His workshop has also become a place where visitors can experience traditional tea making. The opportunities extend beyond individual businesses. Jingmai Mountain received 694,300 tourist visits in 2025, with culture and tourism revenue reaching 563 million yuan ($84.45 million). Residents have converted traditional homes into tea shops, restaurants and guesthouses, retaining the buildings' distinctive appearance while finding new uses for them. The younger generation is adding new partners to these networks. Xia Haoling, who previously worked in branding and new media in Shanghai, settled on Jingmai Mountain and established the Zhishan brand, developing scented sachets and incense inspired by local plants and Blang culture. The growing business has changed everyday logistics, too. Previously, tea sold online had to be packed late into the night and taken down to the township for dispatch the next morning. Couriers now come up to the village regularly to collect parcels. For Xianjin, the ancient forests remain the starting point of these new ventures. "These roots belong to all of us, whichever ethnic group we come from," she said.

item.title: China's first offshore carbon injection project advances, targeting 1.75 million cubic meters of CO2 daily
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 20:37:00
The carbon capture, utilization and storage project at the Dongfang 1-1 gas field in South China's Hainan Province. Photo: Xinhua China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) on Friday announced that the 17,000-ton central platform for a carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) project at the Dongfang 1-1 gas field has been loaded onto a vessel, marking the completion of onshore construction and the start of offshore transportation and installation. Once operational, the project will be able to purify up to 1.75 million cubic meters of carbon dioxide (CO2) per day and permanently store more than 1 million tons of CO2 underground annually. The platform has been loaded onto a vessel and is scheduled for offshore installation in December. The CCUS project is the country's first demonstration project for the application of offshore carbon injection technology to boost natural gas production. Located in the Yinggehai waters in the northern South China Sea, the Dongfang 1-1 gas field is China's largest self-operated offshore gas field. Since starting production in 2003, it has produced over 50 billion cubic meters of natural gas. As the field enters the middle and later stages of development, natural gas output has gradually declined while associated CO2 content has continued to rise, creating the need for innovative solutions, China Media Group reported on Friday. The new CCUS central platform, standing more than 28-stories tall and has a total deck area of over 10,000 square meters, establishes a complete closed-loop system for offshore CO2 capture, purification, storage, and gas displacement. All key equipment is domestically produced. Energy consumption is 20 percent lower than traditional processes, and natural gas recovery rates are improved by more than 12 percent, according to CNOOC. Carbon injection technology for enhanced gas recovery is a branch of the broader CCUS technology system. Its core principle is to turn CO2 produced during natural gas extraction from waste into a resource by capturing, purifying and pressurizing it before reinjecting it into gas-bearing formations. The injected CO2 then acts as a driving force to displace and recover hard-to-extract natural gas. After being put into operation, the platform will connect with 12 other facilities in the Yingge waters area. An industry insider told the Global Times that China's coastal provinces account for roughly half of China's CO2 emissions, yet suitable onshore storage sites nearby are limited. "Marine geological storage is therefore an essential pathway for emission reduction. The Dongfang 1-1 project is not only extending the life of a mature gas field but also paving the way for the expansion of China's offshore CCUS capabilities," said the insider. China previously deployed the country's first offshore oilfield CCUS project at Enping 15-1 oilfield in waters near the Pearl River and the first offshore gas field carbon capture and storage project at Ledong 15-1 gas field, also in Hainan. Global Times

item.title: Takaichi claims to stick to bilateral diplomatic document with China, but does not amount to retraction of erroneous remarks: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 20:15:00
Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi speaks to the media during a press conference on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, on November 19, 2026. Photo: VCG Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's latest remarks on Taiwan have done little to ease concerns over Tokyo's approach to the Taiwan question, as she reiterated that Japan's stance on China's Taiwan is "unchanged," while refusing to clarify or retract her erroneous remarks regarding the island of Taiwan a year ago. A Chinese expert said Takaichi is trying to balance pressure to stabilize ties with China against the need to retain domestic right-wing support, but without concrete corrective action, this approach will do little to improve bilateral relations. Speaking at a news conference on Thursday after she attended the APEC Shenzhen meeting, Takaichi brought up the four documents signed when Japan and China normalized relations in 1972. "The status of the four basic documents between Japan and China remains completely unchanged," she claimed, Japanese media Asahi Shimbun reported. "Japan's basic position on Taiwan is as stated in the Japan-China Joint Communique," Takaichi said. "There has been absolutely no change in this position." However, when asked whether Japan would intervene in a conflict over China's Taiwan, Takaichi declined to elaborate, saying she could not answer hypothetical questions, according to Reuters. The Sino-Japanese Joint Statement notes that the Government of Japan "fully understands and respects" the position of the Chinese government that Taiwan is an inalienable part of the territory of the People's Republic of China. However, Takaichi has not retold the specific requirements from the Sino-Japanese Joint Statement, and experts said this did not amount to a retraction of her previous erroneous comments. When asked to comment on Takaichi's remarks in Shenzhen that the Japanese government's position on China's Taiwan had not changed since 1972, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular press conference on Friday that honoring the four political documents between China and Japan is a political responsibility and legal obligation that the Japanese side must fulfill, and that this must be reflected not only in statements but also in actions. Guo said Japan's immediate priority should be to promptly correct its erroneous words and deeds on the Taiwan question. What is important is to adopt a correct attitude toward historical issues, and what is fundamental is to truly develop an objective and rational perception of China, Guo added. Lü Chao, an expert at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times on Friday that plainly claiming to stick to diplomatic documents while refusing to correct erroneous remarks was an attempt to have it both ways. Takaichi was attempting to balance competing political pressures: responding to China's growing international influence and calls from Japan's business community and people advocating stable bilateral ties, while retaining support from right-wing political constituencies at home, he added. The contradictory statements also appeared to reflect an effort to maintain ambiguity between Japan's diplomatic commitments and its practical security moves, raising concerns about Japan's evolving security policy, Lü added. Recently, Japan has continued to strengthen its so-called "defense capabilities" and expand military buildup. Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said on November 8 that the government will consider organizational reforms to break down traditional barriers among the Ground, Maritime and Air Self-Defense Forces to strengthen the military. The Japanese government plans to approve a revised version of the country's three key security documents in December. For a country with a history of militarist aggression in Asia, any expansion of military capabilities beyond legitimate defense needs warrants close scrutiny, Lü said, warning that such a trajectory could undermine regional security and stability. During the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and US heads of state on Thursday, the Chinese leader said the three countries remember their history of fighting side by side during World War II and stressed the need to cherish the hard-won peace. Major countries should take seriously the legitimate security concerns of all nations, he said, Xinhua News Agency reported. Lü said the groundbreaking meeting sent an important signal about the need to uphold the postwar international order, adding that Japan, as a defeated country in World War II, should reflect on its history and strictly abide by the international rules established after the war. China-Japan relations remain strained over Takaichi's erroneous remarks concerning Taiwan, with tensions already affecting economic and trade ties, people-to-people exchanges and other areas. According to data released on Wednesday by the Japan National Tourism Organization, visitor arrivals from the Chinese mainland plunged 47 percent year-on-year to 379,500 in October, marking the 11th consecutive monthly decline. Lü said that if Tokyo genuinely wants to improve relations with Beijing, it must first correct its erroneous Taiwan-related remarks and demonstrate through concrete actions that it respects the political foundation of bilateral relations. Without substantive corrective action, it will remain difficult for Tokyo's calls for dialogue and strategic reciprocity to translate into tangible improvements in bilateral relations, he added.

item.title: Kazakhstan receives Y-9E transport aircraft from China, with expert seeing wider export potential
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 20:13:00
Y-9E transport aircraft Photo: Courtesy of AVIC SAIC Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry officially announced on Thursday that a Y-9E military transport aircraft has arrived in Almaty, joining the fleet of the military transport aviation of the Kazakhstan Armed Forces. A military affairs expert told the Global Times that the Chinese-made aircraft's mature technology, logistical advantages and competitive cost could give it promising prospects in the international market. The delivery was carried out as part of a planned renewal of the aircraft fleet. The new aircraft will expand capabilities for transporting personnel, military cargo, and materiel, according to a statement published on the ministry's website. In terms of its capabilities, the Y-9E occupies an intermediate position between the C-295, a European-made tactical transport aircraft, and the A400M, a European four-engine military transport aircraft, currently in service. Its arrival will allow more flexible planning of air transport operations based on route distance and cargo weight, according to the release. The Global Times learned that the Y-9E is an export-oriented transport aircraft developed from China's Y-9 platform to meet the requirements of overseas customers. It is designed to transport personnel, equipment and supplies, and features a long range, a spacious cargo compartment, substantial payload capacity and convenient loading and unloading. It can operate in challenging environments, including extreme heat, high altitudes and extreme cold. Publicly available information indicates that the Y-9E is approximately 36 meters long, with a wingspan of about 38 meters. It has a maximum payload of 20 metric tons and a maximum takeoff weight of approximately 65 tons. The aircraft has a maximum level-flight speed of around 660 kilometers per hour, a cruising altitude of 7,000 to 8,000 meters and a maximum range of 5,200 kilometers. The Y-9E is a further development of the Y-8 transport aircraft, with substantial improvements to its airframe structure, Wang Ya'nan, editor-in-chief of Beijing-based Aerospace Knowledge magazine, told the Global Times on Friday. The aircraft features a modern glass cockpit with upgraded avionics that meet mainstream international standards. The aircraft has also benefited from improvements in engine performance and aerodynamics, resulting in an increased payload capacity compared with the Y-8. The aircraft has been showcased at several international and domestic air shows and defense exhibitions, including the 2018 Singapore Airshow, the 15th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition in Zhuhai, South China's Guangdong Province, in 2024, and the 2026 Africa Aerospace and Defence exhibition. Kazakhstan is the second known overseas customer for the Y-9E, following Namibia. In December 2024, the Namibian Air Force officially received two Y-9E medium military transport aircraft bought from China, according to the local media outlet The Namibian. One of the Y-9E's advantages in the export market is the fact that the Chinese People's Liberation Army itself operates the Y-9 in substantial numbers, with various special-mission aircraft also developed on the same platform, Wang said. This large domestic user base helps support higher production volumes, a mature technological foundation and a stable supply of spare parts and maintenance services, while also offering potential cost advantages to overseas customers. The expert added that the Y-9E could offer an alternative to countries seeking to replace aging medium-sized transport aircraft, such as the US-made C-130 Hercules. The C-130 has been in service for decades, but many countries seem to face the challenge of upgrading or replacing their aging fleets. Against this backdrop, the Y-9E offers another option for countries seeking a medium-sized military transport aircraft. Its performance may have won favor in many countries, potentially opening up broader opportunities for the Chinese aircraft in the international market, Wang said.

item.title: China, US militaries hold working group meeting, annual talks under maritime military security consultation mechanism
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 17:47:00
CHINA / DIPLOMACY China, US militaries hold working group meeting, annual talks under maritime military security consultation mechanism By Global Times Published: Nov 20, 2026 05:47 PM
The Chinese and US militaries held the second working group meeting of 2026 and the annual meeting under the China-US maritime military security consultation mechanism in Shanghai, China from November 18 to 20, according to China's Ministry of National Defense. The meetings aimed to implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and promote the sound, stable and sustainable development of military-to-military relations. The two sides held candid, practical and constructive discussions on the current maritime and air security situation between China and the US, reviewed the annual execution of the Rules of Behavior for Safety of Air and Maritime Encounters and discussed measures to improve maritime military security between the two countries, according to China's Ministry of National Defense. They agreed on the agenda for the 2027 working group meeting.

item.title: Chinese boys, aged 14 and 3, set BMX and cartwheel records for Guinness World Records Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 17:28:00
Liu Haoran November 19 marked the 22nd annual Guinness World Records Day. Challengers from around the world pushed the limits of human capability once again on the same day. Among them, two challengers from China attracted considerable attention: a 14-year-old who performed 10 consecutive flips in the air while riding a BMX bike, and a 3-year-old who performed 55 cartwheels in one minute on the ground. In China, 14-year-old BMX freestyle rider Liu Haoran set two records during this year's Guinness World Records Day challenge: "Most consecutive BMX side somersaults" (10 consecutive flips) and "Highest BMX backflip" (3.13 meters). Liu also improved on his own previous world record. A BMX backflip is a freestyle trick in which the rider and bike rotate 360 degrees backward mid-air off a ramp or jump before landing on the wheels. The flair is a highly difficult maneuver in BMX freestyle. Riders must launch themselves into the air on a ramp, simultaneously flipping themselves and their bikes sideways before landing precisely back down the ramp. Peng Yizhou The other challenger from China, Peng Yizhou, 3, a martial arts school student, completed 55 sidecar flips in one minute during this year's challenge, setting a Guinness World Record for the most cartwheels in one minute in the under 16 category. Peng was born in Tangyin County, Anyang City, Central China's Henan Province. His parents are both martial arts instructors. From the age of 7 months, Peng lived with his parents at a martial arts school, watching the older students practice martial arts. At the age of 2, he began to imitate cartwheels on his own and gradually learned to perform the movement independently under his father's guidance. In addition to cartwheels, he also enjoys swimming, playing with toys, and participating in activities with the older students at the martial arts school. For Peng, the cartwheel wasn't initially a competitive skill he needed to master; rather, it stemmed from curiosity and imitation of his surroundings. His parents recalled that when Peng first completed a cartwheel independently, he tried repeatedly, falling several times, until finally landing steadily and excitedly turning to his father, shouting, "Dad, I stood up!" Global Times

item.title: Looking forward to Asia-Pacific cooperation soaring high and far on a boundless journey: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 01:41:00
This photo taken on November 16, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province with APEC elements. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: VCG The historic gathering of APEC members in Shenzhen will become a new starting point for their joint efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community. From here, the vision of Asia-Pacific cooperation will take flight, transforming the collective strength forged within the conference halls into sustained momentum for regional cooperation in the years ahead. "China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation. We would like to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community." Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, and delivered important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle." Focusing on new opportunities and challenges facing the Asia-Pacific region and the world, the Chinese leader, for the first time in the history of APEC, systematically expounded China's proposition on what kind of Asia-Pacific community to build and how to build it, and reaffirmed China's steadfast commitment to supporting Asia-Pacific cooperation, while demonstrating a great sense of responsibility and a global vision in leading and promoting cooperation both within the Asia-Pacific and across the globe. More than three decades ago, APEC was born as the times required, embarking on a grand journey toward building an Asia-Pacific community. Over the past 30-plus years, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone profound transformations, creating an "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. Today, the region has become an anchor of stability for global development. Whether the Asia-Pacific can continue to write this success story concerns not only the general well-being of the economies within the region but also the broader landscape of world peace and development. Faced with this pressing question of the times, the leaders and representatives of 21 economies convened in Shenzhen to chart the course for the future of Asia-Pacific cooperation. This marks the first time in recent years that a full "family photo" of APEC members has been realized, a clear testament to the shared aspiration of all parties for mutually beneficial cooperation. The Chinese side proposed that, in the face of new opportunities and challenges, Asia-Pacific cooperation must adapt to the new realities, take new strides, and open up new prospects and strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. As an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, China is willing to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in strengthening the pillar of economy and trade, upgrading the pillar of connectivity, fostering the pillar of innovation and enhancing the pillar of development. The economy and trade pillar serves as the bedrock and the essential foundation for Asia-Pacific cooperation. The connectivity pillar is a vital support, having effectively underpinned nearly half of the region's cooperative endeavors over the past 12 years. The innovation pillar serves as the primary engine for growth, driving the digital, intelligent, and green transformation of the Asia-Pacific region. The development pillar embodies a people-centered value orientation and offers the key to resolving complex challenges inherent in globalization and regional economic integration. These four pillars complement and reinforce one another, collectively supporting the edifice of an Asia-Pacific community. The Asia-Pacific is where China has its roots and where its future lies. To support Asia-Pacific cooperation, China has introduced a series of concrete supporting measures: providing funding to support APEC practical cooperation, establishing a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies, and setting up cooperation institutions in areas such as digital technology, cross-border data flows, clean energy, and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. These initiatives impose no exclusionary barriers. Instead, they focus on building platforms, establishing mechanisms, and promoting shared benefits, ensuring that the outcomes of cooperation are visible, tangible, and accessible. China will continue to honor its commitments through concrete actions, working with all parties to ensure that cooperation projects take root and bear fruit. It will inject fresh momentum into the building of an Asia-Pacific community and provide tangible support for the "four pillars" through the provision of more practical public goods. The meeting unanimously adopted the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which put forward the "Shenzhen Vision" for building an Asia-Pacific community, along with three outcome documents covering trade, connectivity, and innovation. As the most significant outcome of the APEC "China Year" and a new milestone in APEC cooperation, the "Shenzhen Vision" reaffirms APEC's role as the primary platform for regional economic cooperation. Guided by the principles of voluntary participation, non-binding arrangements, and consensus-building, it commits to transforming APEC into a more modern, efficient, and pragmatic incubator of ideas. The tides of Shenzhen Bay bear witness to the powerful momentum of Asia-Pacific cooperation. APEC members are transforming their shared commitment to standing together through challenges into tangible connections spanning mountains and oceans. From the Port of Chancay opening new routes for Asia-Pacific supply chains and the Pinglu Canal strengthening land-sea links between southwestern China and Southeast Asia, to Juncao technology taking root in Pacific Island countries; from the Asia-Pacific Model E-Port Network significantly improving the efficiency of cross-border customs clearance and cross-border electricity transmission lines linking the region's clean energy resources, to APEC cooperation zones for small and medium-sized enterprises building bridges that connect countless small and micro businesses to shared markets, these concrete projects are weaving a strong connection. Through practical cooperation, the contours of an Asia-Pacific community are becoming ever clearer and more tangible. Over the past 30-plus years, China and the Asia-Pacific have advanced together, reinforcing each other's development and achieving shared prosperity through openness. Today, as a new chapter begins, China's high-standard opening-up and high-quality development will bring fresh development opportunities to the Asia-Pacific. The historic gathering of APEC members in Shenzhen will become a new starting point for their joint efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community. From here, the vision of Asia-Pacific cooperation will take flight, transforming the collective strength forged within the conference halls into sustained momentum for regional cooperation in the years ahead. Amid a rapidly changing global landscape, this momentum will provide a firm foundation for an Asia-Pacific home that belongs to all its members and is defined by shared prosperity.

item.title: China-Russia-US summit is unprecedented and makes history: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 01:35:00
Photo: Xinhua China, Russia and the US have different national conditions, but this doesn't mean confrontation is inevitable. By communicating in advance, considering issues from one another's perspectives and acting with caution on major sensitive matters involving each other's interests, particularly by refraining from crossing each other's red lines, major powers can indeed avoid the "Thucydides Trap." Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday afternoon held a China-Russia-US summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. President Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace: Major countries should uphold mutual respect, uphold peaceful coexistence, uphold win-win cooperation, and uphold dialogue and consultation. The four "upholds" outline a clear path and set of rules for building a new model of major-country relations, and provide important guidance for China, Russia, and the US to strengthen strategic communication and practical cooperation and jointly safeguard world peace. The core agenda of this summit centers on two key dimensions: safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations. These issues not only determine the future trajectory of major-country relations but are also inextricably linked to the vital development interests of nations across the globe. Looking back at the evolution of the international order, humanity has taken many wrong turns in the management of major-country relations. Since modern times, the rise of many emerging powers has been accompanied by intense geopolitical conflicts; the harrowing lessons of the two world wars, for instance, were rooted in zero-sum games played by major powers. Peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos. Forging a new, right path for major countries to get along serves the interests of the three nations and aligns with the expectations of the international community. Can major countries move beyond the narrative of competition and achieve constructive interactions? This is a question that China, Russia and the US must answer. Historically, as the principal victors of the anti-fascist alliance in World War II, the three countries fought side by side to defeat militarism and fascism, laying the foundations for the postwar international order underpinned by the United Nations Charter. Firmly upholding the postwar international order, safeguarding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defending the hard-won achievements of victory in World War II are both a historical responsibility shared by the three countries as victors and a common commitment to all peace-loving nations around the world. As major countries of the world and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the US should, and can, set an example by working together to address global challenges, jointly safeguarding world peace and stability. In today's world, the overarching trends of economic globalization and global multipolarity are irreversible, but they are also facing enormous challenges. Against the backdrop of frequent fluctuations in international energy prices and an uneven transition from traditional energy to new-energy sources, the international community is deeply concerned about energy security, the security of shipping routes, and the security of industrial and supply chains. Enhanced communication and coordination among China, Russia, and the US will help prevent major countries from falling into vicious competition over resources, technology, and corridors, help maintain the stability and smooth functioning of energy industrial and supply chains, and help safeguard the stability of the global energy market. China, Russia and the US have different national conditions, but this doesn't mean confrontation is inevitable. By communicating in advance, considering issues from one another's perspectives and acting with caution on major sensitive matters involving each other's interests, particularly by refraining from crossing each other's red lines, major powers can indeed avoid the "Thucydides Trap." The Taiwan question lies at the very core of China's core interests and constitutes the first red line that must not be crossed by any country seeking to develop relations with China. For a long time, the reason "Taiwan independence" separatist forces have repeatedly dared to test the limits of danger is precisely that they have clung to the illusion of exploiting tensions among major countries, attempting to profit from their rivalries. The leaders of China, Russia and the US share common views on safeguarding world peace and have reached a series of important consensuses on maintaining strategic stability and international security. This means that the space in which "Taiwan independence" forces have imagined they could survive by exploiting divisions among major countries is steadily narrowing. Many analysts believe that without China's sustained efforts and its role as the host, this "historic gathering" would probably have been difficult to achieve. While we will not engage in hypothetical analysis, it is undeniable that China played an important role in facilitating the meeting. This is closely linked to China's position as a responsible major country and its diplomatic philosophy of promoting a new model of major-country relations. Both the Russian and US leaders expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic meeting. The meeting represents not only an important milestone in the history of international relations, but also a landmark event in major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics. The China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace released after the summit represents a joint solution of peace provided by the three countries based on both current and future situations. Its provisions on reforming the United Nations, reaffirming the importance of stable energy flows, and emphasizing that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought largely echo the four points made by the Chinese side on how major countries should get along with each other. Certainly, a single meeting cannot resolve every problem. But as long as countries uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, mutually beneficial cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, a way forward can always be found. The China-Russia-US summit in Shenzhen can be seen as a starting point, opening up new possibilities for constructive interactions among major countries and for exploring the right way for them to get along. It also represents an important attempt by major countries to jointly explore constructing a new type of major-country relations in an era of multipolarity. The seeds sown by the meeting of the three heads of state will surely take root, sprout, bloom, and bear fruit.

item.title: GT Voice: South Korea may face new test after hitting $1 trillion export milestone
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 22:39:00
Visitors check out ship models at a booth during the Offshore Korea 2026 held in Busan, South Korea on October 14, 2026. Photo: VCG South Korea's exports so far this year surpassed $1 trillion for the first time as of Thursday, according to local media reports, which said that the country had become the fourth country in the world to reach the milestone. The achievement reflects the country's manufacturing strength and global demand for its products, particularly semiconductors. But sustaining that success may depend on more than technological competitiveness. According to The Korea Herald, South Korea is the first new entrant to the trillion-dollar export club in 19 years. What has changed to make this possible now? One answer lies in the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom. South Korea appears to have seized this opportunity well, establishing itself as an important export base for memory chips as demand for AI hardware takes off. Its semiconductor exports nearly tripled in the January-October period this year, accounting for 43 percent of the country's total exports. The question now is whether South Korea can sustain this momentum. Calls for export diversification are understandable, given the country's heavy reliance on semiconductors. But diversification alone may not be enough to secure the next phase of growth. The advent of AI represents a historic opportunity, creating a scale of global demand that few other industries are likely to match, at least in the near term. Rather than treating its reliance on semiconductors simply as a vulnerability to be reduced, South Korea may need to build on its current advantage and further deepen its role in the global semiconductor supply chain. One way to deepen that role is to support AI development in the markets that buy South Korean chips. There are growing concerns in South Korea that its export success and the resulting trade surpluses could invite greater scrutiny from some trading partners, including India and Turkey, and put pressure on Seoul to address its trade imbalances. This makes it all the more important for South Korea to demonstrate the broader value of its exports. Helping other economies develop their AI capabilities could make South Korean chips more integral to their technological development and support more lasting demand. But this depends on South Korean chipmakers staying at the technological frontier and offering trading partners their most advanced products as AI requirements evolve. These top-tier chips can help support the development of local AI industries and strengthen South Korea's place in the global semiconductor supply chain. Less advanced products are unlikely to play the same role. That may be easier said than done. Washington increasingly views AI through the lens of global competition. How much freedom will South Korean chipmakers have to sell their most advanced products to other economies without US interference? There is a bad precedent for this. In December 2024, the Korea JoongAng Daily reported that US restrictions on high-bandwidth memory exports to China threatened to choke South Korean chipmakers, jeopardizing some of their most lucrative dynamic random access memory sales to the world's largest semiconductor market. The implications may extend beyond the Chinese market. As Washington treats semiconductors as a strategic industry and uses export controls to protect its advantage in AI, South Korea's expanding chip exports could expose growing differences between the interests of the two economies. Those differences could widen as chip exports help propel South Korea into the trillion-dollar export club. For South Korea, the test may go beyond economics. It will also involve finding room to expand its chip exports amid a complex geopolitical landscape, navigating potential US efforts to intervene more directly in global chip trade, and reaching more customers in developing economies, including China, with its most advanced products. Having joined the trillion-dollar export club, South Korea now ranks among the world's largest exporting economies, giving it greater influence in global trade. It has reason to make its voice heard in support of free trade and to turn that commitment into mutually beneficial trade cooperation with partners around the world. At a critical juncture as the global economy enters the AI era, freer trade and resistance to protectionism and unilateralism can help expand AI-related trade and open up wider markets for South Korean chip exports.
